source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #289 (branch fix/126-resource-limits at head 457b2094d81e43a7452dbe56ba0aacc09c804f7f — branch commits 36fb96d (embedder-configurable resource limits via LimitsConfig (#126)) and 457b209 (enforce the total-page ceiling on host-side memory growth) plus merge commit f77c527 bringing in current main 20e7e94, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45268180814 and 45268200208 against the branch and pull-request run 45268166014, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #289 (#126, embedder-configurable resource limits: RuntimeConfig gains LimitsConfig with the store-wide total-memory ceiling, a per-table element cap, the guest value-stack size, and the JIT code-cache ceiling folded in from JitConfig). The branch merged current main (20e7e94, containing PR #288) before measurement; the merge was conflict-free, but the jit_code_cache regression test added by PR #288 still set the code-cache ceiling through JitConfig and was moved to LimitsConfig::max_code_cache_bytes (that stale reference was the single cause of the first merged-tree CI failures in clippy, feature coverage, and both JIT-test jobs). Review of this PR also moved the total-page ceiling into Memory::grow itself — a shared TotalMemoryBudget that every memory registers with when the store adopts it — after review showed host callbacks growing memory through the public Memory handle bypassed the dispatch-level check. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (20e7e94) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45266215787, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta is this PR's own. The deltas are the cost of the limits machinery in the telomere library: in release, every configuration that links the library grows (stripped file +2,056 B in component and core-nosimd to +3,240 B in wasi-threads; stripped .text +1,664 B to +2,912 B), largest in wasi-threads, where the shared-memory budget paths land; the baseline configuration, which links no telomere code, is byte-identical in both profiles. In release-size the growth is smaller and near-uniform (stripped file +1,120 B to +1,280 B; stripped .text +848 B to +1,056 B). Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is the release component stripped file series at +9.58% (2,433,656 B to 2,666,816 B), up from +9.50%; the core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
